solutions.explanation:
An exponent of \(-1\) means to take a reciprocal. First, \(x\ne0\) and \(y\ne0\) are required. Combining the terms inside the parentheses gives
\[
x^{-1}+y^{-1}=\frac1x+\frac1y=\frac{x+y}{xy}.
\]
The outer reciprocal also requires this sum to be nonzero, so \(x+y\ne0\). We can now invert the fraction:
\[
(x^{-1}+y^{-1})^{-1}
=\left(\frac{x+y}{xy}\right)^{-1}
=\frac{xy}{x+y}.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{\dfrac{xy}{x+y}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\), retaining all three original restrictions.
solutions.title: Add first, then take the reciprocal
